scenes.visualIntent: Problem-first hook showing forward prices depend on replication cost, not spot forecasts
keyElements: Forward prices are pinned by replication costs, not market guesses
No-arbitrage means identical future cash flows carry identical prices today
Overpriced forwards trigger instant cash-and-carry profits

scenes.visualIntent: Contrast investment assets and consumption assets to explain two-sided vs upper bounds
keyElements: Investment assets allow two-sided arbitrage equality
Consumption assets cannot easily be shorted physically
Short-sale limits give consumption assets an upper bound only

scenes.visualIntent: Causal chain of borrowing shares, paying intermediate dividends, and closing the short
keyElements: Short selling borrows unowned shares to raise immediate spot cash
Short sellers must compensate lenders for all intermediate dividends
Forward delivery returns borrowed shares to close the position

scenes.visualIntent: Derive F0 = S0 exp(rT) and define cash-and-carry arbitrage
keyElements: Non-income forward price compounds spot at risk-free rate: F0 = S0 exp(rT)
Overpriced forwards trigger cash-and-carry arbitrage
Financing cost r pins forward value strictly above spot

scenes.visualIntent: Compute exact 1-year forward price on a dividend-paying stock with prediction prompt
keyElements: Subtract dividend present value I from spot before compounding
Forward buyers forfeit dividends paid before expiration
Adjusted spot $58.00 grows at 5.0% to fair price $60.97

scenes.visualIntent: Trace step-by-step reverse cash-and-carry arbitrage when F0 < S0 exp(rT)
keyElements: Underpriced forwards trigger reverse cash-and-carry arbitrage
Shorting spot and investing proceeds funds future delivery
Riskless surplus lifts depressed forward quotes back to fair value

scenes.visualIntent: Compare discrete dividend PV adjustment I against continuous dividend yield q
keyElements: Discrete dividends subtract cash present value I from spot
Continuous dividend yield q adjusts net carry rate to (r - q)
Higher dividend yield reduces the theoretical forward price

scenes.visualIntent: Distinguish contractual delivery price K, market forward F0, and mark-to-market value f
keyElements: Delivery price K stays locked at inception when initial value f = 0
Market forward price F0 shifts continuously as spot prices evolve
Long contract value equals discounted difference f = (F0 - K) exp(-rT)

scenes.visualIntent: Contrast novice pricing myths against no-arbitrage replication and forward-futures convergence
keyElements: Forward quotes do not measure subjective expectations of future spot
Forward and futures prices match identically under constant rates
Positive rate correlation slightly lifts futures prices over forwards

scenes.visualIntent: 3-beat interactive quiz calculating arbitrage profit on a $100 stock quoted at $108.00
keyElements: Spot $100 compounded 1 year at 5.0% gives fair forward $105.13
Market quote $108.00 exceeds fair value by $2.87
Borrow cash, buy spot, and short forward to capture $2.87

scenes.visualIntent: Synthesize Part 1 valuation principles and bridge forward to Chapter 5 Part 2 macro assets
keyElements: No-arbitrage replication enforces tight bounds on investment assets
Dividends and yields reduce forward carry costs proportionally
Part 2 extends pricing to index arbitrage, FX parity, and commodities

scenes.visualIntent: Fixed 6-beat summary codifying all 8 core forward pricing rules taught in Part 1
keyElements: No-arbitrage replication enforces pricing across investment assets
Cash dividends and yields adjust carry directly
Delivery price K fixes at entry while value f floats
